newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-LEVERKUSEN PULL OUT OF SERGIO MOVE TO ROMA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LEVERKUSEN PULL OUT OF SERGIO MOVE TO ROMA.

text.p: Bayer Leverkusen have pulled out of a deal to sell Brazilian midfielder Paulo Sergio to Italy's AS Roma, the German sports news agency SID reported on Friday.
The move was a reaction to a FIFA decision on Wednesday that will allow all out-of-contract foreign players to move between clubs within the European Union on free transfers.

Out-of-contract EU nationals have been able to move between clubs in the Union without a transfer fee since the European Court of Justice's "Bosman ruling" of 1995. But the FIFA decision extended these rights to all players in the EU, regardless of nationality.

Leverkusen and Roma had agreed on a move in January this year for a fee expected to be around six or seven million marks ($3.6 million to $4.6 million). Under the new FIFA ruling, the payment would no longer have been required.
The Bundesliga side has taken advantage of a special clause in players' contracts in Germany which allows clubs to retain a player for an extra year if the transfer system changes.
Leverkusen general manager Reiner Calmund said he did not fear any legal problems. "The matter's settled as far as we're concerned," he said.
